segmentation.text: In no case shall any part of any vehicle
part of the load of such vehicle
or trailer
attached to such vehicle
project into the street more than fifteen feet measured on a line at right angles to the curb.

elements.justification: "any vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed whole and never expanded into classes. "any part of" the vehicle is any point of its body, whose size kin.extent carries ("the body's size along its axes about the reference point"), so the farthest point of the body is what the bound reads. "In no case" admits no exception.

"trailer" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer ("a vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle or recreational vehicle, that is without motor power, is designed and constructed to be drawn by a motor vehicle"), claimed whole: the trailer is judged as a road user of its own, its body read by the same bound.

"part of the load of such vehicle" is read through the outline the source reports for the vehicle's body, kin.extent ("the body's size along its axes about the reference point"): a load carried on the vehicle within that outline is judged with it; a load overhanging the reported outline is not seen, as the narrowing on span s5 discloses.

"project" states where a standing body stands out into the street, in a section of the chapter on stopping, standing and parking: it is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, drv.motion.parked ("Road user a is parked: \"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation"); the narrowing discloses the reading. "street" is DEF-NRS-484A-265 ("the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city", not an aggregate): st.highway ("the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders"); its "not a stand-in for: the roadway" clause is respected since the definition names the entire width; rel.occupies ("a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region") anchors the vehicle on its own street, as the mapping index reads "upon a street"; the city limits are the ordinance's own territorial scope. "more than fifteen feet" is the stated figure (literal): the body's projection, the ground distance from the curb to its outline (st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it") plus the body's own extent across the curb line (kin.extent, "a formula reads the full length, width and height"), is compared with it. "the curb" is st.road_edge ("curb or edge of the roadway") lying on the vehicle's street (st.on_way, "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on"); the curb the vehicle stands at is the road edge of that street nearest its body (st.region_geometry ground distance). "on a line at right angles to the curb": the curb runs along the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies (st.lane_direction, "direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region), so the body's extent at right angles to the curb is its length (kin.extent) times the absolute cross product of its heading (kin.heading, read normalised) with that direction plus its width times their absolute dot product. The sign of the direction does not matter. st.lane_direction is not used as a manoeuvre or a path: only its line is read; the narrowing on this span discloses the reading.

residues.why: A trailer is itself "a vehicle" by its definition DEF-LVMC-11-02-170, so the duty binds its body through "any vehicle" whether or not it is attached; attachment adds no restriction.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle or a trailer (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer), is parked at the observation (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.parking_min_duration)) and its footprint overlaps a highway h (rel.occupies subject h, st.highway): it stands in a street.
obligation: For every highway h the subject occupies (rel.occupies), every road edge c (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way c h) whose ground distance from the subject's body (st_region_geometry_distance) is at most that of every other road edge lying on h (the curb the vehicle stands at), and every travel region r (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the ground distance from the subject's body to c, plus the subject's length (kin_extent length) times the absolute value of the cross product of its heading (kin_heading x, y) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction x, y), plus its width (kin_extent width) times the absolute value of their dot product, is at most fifteen feet (literal 15 ft). Where r carries no direction, the heading or the geometry is unobserved, the sum is unknown.

narrowings.why: "project" is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, parked (at rest for p.parking_min_duration): a vehicle travelling or halted briefly in traffic is not judged, though the words name no state of motion; the section sits among the stopping, standing and parking rules and measures from the curb a vehicle stands at. A load is judged only within the body outline the source reports; a load overhanging that outline is not seen.

The curb's line is read as the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies, and the curb as the road edge of its street nearest its body; the projection is the body-to-curb distance plus the body's extent across that line, which assumes the body lies on the street side of the curb.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A truck 10 m long is parked for 10 minutes at right angles to the curb of a two-lane street, 0.2 m from the curb; its heading is perpendicular to the roadway's direction, so its body reaches about 10.2 m into the street, beyond fifteen feet.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car 1.8 m wide is parked for 10 minutes parallel to the curb, 0.3 m from it, heading along the roadway's direction: its body reaches about 2.1 m into the street.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car travels at 12 m/s along the far lane of the street, 8 m from the curb: it is not parked, so the rule does not apply.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A truck is parked at right angles to the curb, but the source maps regions without their outline (st.region_geometry absent): the distance from the body to the curb is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A detached trailer 8 m long is parked for 10 minutes at right angles to the curb, 0.1 m from it: as a vehicle in its own right its body reaches about 8.1 m into the street.

segmentation.text: The City Traffic Engineer shall determine upon what streets angle parking shall be permitted,
and shall provide signage or other markings to indicate where such parking is permitted.
Where angle parking is permitted,
no person shall stand or park a vehicle unless the front of the vehicle is pointed toward the direction of lawful traffic movement.

elements.justification: The Traffic Engineer's determination of the streets where angle parking is permitted is a legal status no scene shows; the next words name its evidence, the signage or markings. It is read through them: a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code ... angle_parking") governing (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") the travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), or a marked parking bay (st.parking_space, "marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute") whose angle stands clear of zero. The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre (its not-a-stand-in clause).

"signage" is the angle_parking regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign) governing (dev.governs) the travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); "other markings" is a marked bay (st.parking_space, "marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute") the vehicle occupies whose angle (st_parking_space_angle) stands clear of zero by more than the source's angle resolution. Their presence is the evidence of the permission they indicate.

"Where angle parking is permitted" is the place the signage or markings indicate: a travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that an angle_parking sign governs (dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs), or that the vehicle occupies together with an angled marked bay (st.parking_space with its angle clear of zero). Presence of the feature, no size bound: the angle is read only against the source's resolution.

"no person shall stand or park a vehicle" has the same words and meaning as the mapping index's "No person shall stand or park a vehicle" (LVMC_11_52_040_A): drv.motion.parked ("Road user a is parked: \"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\"") with the standing duration as its window, covering standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle ... otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers") and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155); "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole. "No person" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. "unless the front ...": same words as the mapping index's "headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement" (LVMC_11_52_040_A): "the front of the vehicle" points along kin.heading ("direction the body points"; not its velocity, so a standing vehicle has one); "the direction of lawful traffic movement" is the direction designated for traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, claimed whole as the word's admitted aggregate) on the travel region the vehicle occupies: st.lane_direction ("direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in"), read on that region (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "pointed toward" is a positive dot product of the heading with that direction.

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region r (st.travel_region) where angle parking is permitted: a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign) governs r (dev.governs), or the subject also occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle (st_parking_space_angle), in absolute value, exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.
obligation: Where the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.standing_min_duration)), for every travel region r it occupies that is selected as in the applicability (governed by an angle_parking sign, or occupied together with an angled parking space), the dot product of the subject's heading (kin_heading) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction) is positive: the front of the vehicle points toward the direction of lawful traffic movement. A subject that is not parked complies. Where r carries no direction or the heading is unobserved, the verdict is unknown.

narrowings.why: The Traffic Engineer's determination is a legal status read through the signage or markings that display it: a determination no sign or marking displays is not read.

The duty to provide signage or markings is the Engineer's and is not judged on a trace; the presence of the angle_parking sign or the angled marked bay is read as the indication of where angle parking is permitted.

"the direction of lawful traffic movement" is read as the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies at the angle-parking place; a vehicle wholly inside a bay that overlaps no travel region is not judged.

scenarios.name: forbid

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car stands for 5 minutes in the same angled bay with its heading 45 degrees off the lane's direction, pointing forward with traffic: the dot product with the lane's direction is positive.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car is parked parallel to the curb on a street with no angle_parking sign and no angled bay: the rule does not apply.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is parked in an angled bay at an angle_parking sign, but the source does not supply headings (kin.heading absent): where its front points is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car pulls into the angled bay heading against the lane's direction, halts 20 seconds to let a passenger out and leaves: it neither stands nor parks for the standing duration.

segmentation.text: No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or a traffic control device,
in any of the following places:
Within fifteen feet of an intersection.

elements.justification: "stop" here is prohibited, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies by its own scope ("when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not"); standing and parking are halts too, so the three together are any halt: drv.motion.complete_halt ("The road user is at rest at the observation"), a state at one observation, not an act over time. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole. "No person" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"other traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"), claimed whole for a road user other than the subject; rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places it ahead of the halted vehicle and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") measures the gap the operationalization bounds; a centre distance would overstate it (rel.centre_distance's not-a-stand-in clause).

Nearest atoms only: the device atoms carry the halts a device directs (read on span p6), not a halt that another law requires of the vehicle (yielding to a pedestrian, stopping for a school bus or an emergency vehicle, at a railway crossing); no atom or operator decides that some engaged rule requires the halt the vehicle makes. The span is a gap.

Same mapping as the index's "unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer": dev.human_direction ("a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}") with role police_officer and indication stop, governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs is read as control of that region, not as the place of the halt (its not-a-stand-in clause). "police officer" (DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer.

"the directions of ... a traffic control device" to halt: a stop sign (dev.stop_sign, "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign), a traffic signal (dev.traffic_signal) showing circular_red, a red_arrow, flashing_red or circular_yellow, or a railway signal or gate (dev.railway_signal_or_gate) with lights flashing or gate not up, governing (dev.governs) a travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). Each device is read by its own state; a sign is not a signal. Its official status is presumed from its presence.

"an intersection" (DEF-NRS-484A-105, "the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways"; an alley junction is none) is st.intersection ("the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection"). "Within fifteen feet of" is the ground distance from the vehicle's body to it, st.region_geometry ("the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)"), which anchors the vehicle; occupancy is not read (its not-a-stand-in clause) since the words state a distance.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing: a halt with a road user of traffic ahead in the same lane within the body gap of halted vehicles in a queue is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), has its body within fifteen feet (literal 15 ft) of an intersection: some st.intersection region i with st_region_geometry_distance(subject, i) at most fifteen feet. None of the exceptions holds at the observation: no road user o of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, not the subject) is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; no police officer's direction to stop (dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop) governs a travel region the subject occupies; no stop sign, yield sign, traffic signal showing a red or yellow indication, or flashing railway signal or lowered gate governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); and the halt is not one another law requires (gap on span p4).
obligation: The subject is not at rest: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold at the observation.

narrowings.why: "necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only through a road user of traffic ahead of the vehicle in its lane within the queue gap; a halt for crossing traffic that is not ahead in the lane is not read as necessary.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts 2 m short of an intersection's edge with no road user ahead of it, no officer and no device governing its lane, and stays at rest; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives through the stretch 2 m short of the intersection at 8 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car halts 40 m from the nearest intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car halts near an intersection, but the source maps regions without outlines (st.region_geometry absent): whether it is within fifteen feet is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car halts 2 m short of the intersection behind another car halted 2 m ahead of it in the same lane: a halt in a queue of traffic.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the stop line 1 m short of the intersection where a stop sign governs its lane.

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: queue spacing (jam density) of urban traffic-flow studies

gaps.proposal: `Formula.requiredByRuleSet (who : Arg)`: true at an observation where some rule of the set, engaged there for road user `who`, requires of it the conduct it shows there (here a halt), so that the conduct is in compliance with law; false where no engaged rule requires it; unknown where an engaged rule's requirement is unknown. It decides whether a halt is one another law requires (yielding to a pedestrian, stopping for a school bus or an emergency vehicle, before a sidewalk when emerging from a driveway, at a railway crossing), which the words except from the prohibition.
gaps.nearest: Formula.rule and Formula.ruleApplies compose one named rule and read its verdict or its engagement: neither ranges over the rules of the set nor says that a rule requires the conduct shown; the device atoms (dev.stop_sign, dev.traffic_signal, dev.governs) carry only the halts a device directs.

with other traffic

or a traffic control device,

operationalizations.standard: in or near a private driveway
operationalizations.convention: one passenger-car length of frontage: a vehicle parked with its body within that ground distance of the driveway is parked near it

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), has its body in front of or within five feet (literal 5 ft) of a public or private driveway: for a driveway entrance e (gap: no atom tells a driveway's entrance from an alley's; nearest st.driveway_or_alley_entrance), st_region_geometry_distance(subject, e) is at most five feet. None of the exceptions holds at the observation: no road user o of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, not the subject) is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; no police officer's direction to stop (dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop) governs a travel region the subject occupies; no stop sign, yield sign, traffic signal showing a red or yellow indication, or flashing railway signal or lowered gate governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); the halt is not one another law requires (gap on span p4); it is not the parking (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.parking_min_duration), within p.driveway_near_reach of a private driveway, of a vehicle controlled by the driveway's owner or controller or a family member or invitee (gap on span d4); and the subject is not a United States Postal Service vehicle halted on its business (gap on span d5).
obligation: The subject is not at rest: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold at the observation.

narrowings.why: "necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only through a road user of traffic ahead of the vehicle in its lane within the queue gap; a halt for crossing traffic that is not ahead in the lane is not read as necessary.
"being operated on official business" is a purpose read through the postal vehicle's halt at the place itself: every halt of such a vehicle there is taken as made on its business.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts across the mouth of a residential driveway, its body overlapping the entrance, with no road user ahead and no device or officer governing its lane, and stays at rest; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives past the driveway at 8 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the curb 15 m from the nearest driveway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car halts near a driveway, but the source maps regions without outlines (st.region_geometry absent): whether it is within five feet is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car halts 1 m from a driveway behind a car halted 2 m ahead of it in the same lane: a halt in a queue of traffic.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of object-tracking and vehicle-dynamics recordings

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: queue spacing (jam density) of urban traffic-flow studies

param_proposals.name: p.parking_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as temporary, as for loading or unloading: a common time limit of a passenger loading zone
param_proposals.source: municipal passenger loading zone time limits

param_proposals.name: p.driveway_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a parked vehicle's body to a private driveway within which it is parked near that driveway: about one passenger-car length of the frontage the driveway serves
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design vehicle length (AASHTO P vehicle, about 5.8 m)

gaps.proposal: `Formula.requiredByRuleSet (who : Arg)`: true at an observation where some rule of the set, engaged there for road user `who`, requires of it the conduct it shows there (here a halt), so that the conduct is in compliance with law; false where no engaged rule requires it; unknown where an engaged rule's requirement is unknown. It decides whether a halt is one another law requires (yielding to a pedestrian, stopping before the sidewalk on emerging from a driveway, for a school bus or an emergency vehicle), which the words except from the prohibition.
gaps.nearest: Formula.rule and Formula.ruleApplies compose one named rule and read its verdict or its engagement: neither ranges over the rules of the set nor says that a rule requires the conduct shown; the device atoms (dev.stop_sign, dev.traffic_signal, dev.governs) carry only the halts a device directs.

gaps.proposal: `st.driveway_entrance` | the place where a driveway, a way used for vehicular travel to a property (in private ownership or public), meets the highway, carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary **Not a stand-in for:** an alley's entrance or a private road's | general. It decides where a halt is forbidden: in front of or within the stated distance of a driveway, and not of an alley.
gaps.nearest: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: its not-a-stand-in clause states that the kind does not tell an alley's entrance from a private road's or driveway's, so the forbidden place would be read at every alley entrance.

gaps.proposal: `rel.premises_privilege` | relation: the road user's vehicle is controlled by the person who owns or is in control of a private driveway region, or by a family member or invitee of that person, as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** the vehicle's owner (DEF-NRS-484A-150) or its position | local. It decides whose parking at the driveway the words exempt.
gaps.nearest: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance carries the driveway's place only; no atom records who owns or controls it or the relation of the person parking to that person.

gaps.proposal: `ru.postal_vehicle` | a vehicle of the national postal service, identifiable by its livery **Not a stand-in for:** an official vehicle of another service (`ru.official_vehicle`) | local. It decides which road users the words exempt.
gaps.nearest: ru.official_vehicle: its kinds (tow, utility, highway_maintenance, incident_management, regulatory_agency, coroner, armored_car, municipal, other) carry no postal kind, and kind other does not tell a postal vehicle from any other.
